items.html:
The best exact gradient optimization is one evaluation per unordered particle pair, shared by both directions and by response reconstruction.

Let (C(d)) be a translation block, (d=r_i-r_j), (Z=T^H Y), and (X) the solution. Define (Q) as helicity swap multiplied by ((-1)^l). Existing properties establish

[ C(-d)=Q,C(d),Q,\qquad Q=Q^H=Q^{-1}. ]

This identity is already checked bitwise for block values at plan.rs:475, and analytically for positional/wavenumber derivatives at waves.rs:604.

For each (i<j), combine both directed cotangents:

[ G=Z_iX_j^H+Q(Z_jX_i^H)Q. ]

Then one plan.pullback(k, d, Singular, G) supplies the joint frequency contribution and displacement gradient (g); add (g) to particle (i), subtract it from particle (j). There is no extra minus sign: differentiation through (C(-d)=QC(d)Q) already accounts for it. Current pair_gradients evaluates both directed derivative tables and both table contractions separately.

For one illumination, avoid even forming dense (G): for entry (a,b), feed

[ G_{ab}=Z_{i,a}\overline{X_{j,b}} +s_as_b Z_{j,\bar a}\overline{X_{i,\bar b}} ]

directly into the existing weighted harmonic contraction, where (\bar a) swaps helicity and (s_a=(-1)^{l_a}). This removes the tiny faer outer-product call and dense scratch traffic; it does not reduce the number of angular coupling terms. In current mode order, helicity swap is index ^ 1, and degree is mode_degrees[index / 2] + 1.

A further exact improvement is to fuse response construction with that pair pass. pullback:307 currently computes C X separately before calling pair_gradients; each derivative table already contains translation values at plan.rs:205. Reuse them for

[ R_i \mathrel{+}= C(d)X_j,\qquad R_j \mathrel{+}= Q C(d)QX_i. ]

No persistent pair cache is required. The existing deterministic chunk reduction can accumulate position gradients, plus response vectors if fused. Its memory becomes (O(64,N,M,R)), rather than (O(N^2)); for single RHS this is modest, but many columns/high multipole orders make that constant material.

Expected limits: unordered pairs can roughly halve the pair-gradient work; fusion also removes the separate response coupling pass. Complete-gradient gains are smaller because forward and adjoint GMRES each execute many coupling passes. This is complementary to accelerating the forward operator, not a likely standalone order-of-magnitude win.

A potentially stronger single-RHS opportunity is replacing generic AMOS spherical Hankel evaluation for the cluster’s positive-real arguments with elementary seeds and upward recurrence; I sent that separately. No edits, benchmarks, or Cargo commands were run.
